record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.original_question: If Σ is a topological disk immersed in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle, must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by that circle or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. Is a topological cmc disk spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma$ be a smoothly immersed compact surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is homeomorphic to a closed disk and whose mean curvature is constant. Suppose the boundary $\partial\Sigma$ is mapped to a round circle $C\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ (a planar circle of some positive radius). Prove or disprove: $\Sigma$ must be either the flat planar disk bounded by $C$ or a spherical cap whose boundary is $C$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every immersed CMC topological disk in $\mathbb{R}^3$ spanning a round circle must be a planar disk or a spherical cap is a long-standing open problem. Partial results are known: under additional hypotheses (e.g., embeddedness, the disk lying on one side of the boundary plane, or a free-boundary-type contact angle condition as in Nitsche's theorem) the conclusion holds, but the general immersed case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (López, survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the spherical cap conjecture for CMC surfaces with circular boundary and notes that even the disk case is open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of immersed CMC disks bounded by a circle is an open problem, with only partial results under embeddedness or other restrictions.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary (problem list)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open problem whether a topological CMC disk spanning a circle is a planar disk or a spherical cap.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open in recent surveys of CMC boundary problems.
